title: Smash Burgers
description: Thin patties pressed hard onto a ferociously hot pan so the edges turn lacy and deeply browned, stacked two to a bun with melted cheese and a sharp burger sauce.

steps.text: Stir the burger sauce ingredients together in a small bowl. Prepare the onion, gherkins and lettuce so the toppings are ready before you start cooking.
Divide the mince into 8 equal portions of about 75g and roll each very loosely into a ball. Do not season or compact them. Keep them in the fridge until the pan is hot.
steps.tip: Cold, loosely packed mince smashes into a ragged-edged patty. Overworked mince turns dense and bouncy.

steps.text: Set a cast-iron or heavy-based frying pan over a medium heat and toast the buns cut-side down until golden. Set them aside.
Turn the heat up to high and let the dry pan heat until it is just starting to smoke. Open a window or switch on the extractor fan.

Put 2 or 3 balls of mince in the pan, well spaced. Lay a square of baking paper over each one and press down hard with a sturdy spatula until the patty is about 5mm thick, then peel off the paper. Season generously with salt and pepper and cook without moving until the edges are dark brown and crisp.
steps.tip: Smash within the first 30 seconds only. Pressing later squeezes out the juices.

steps.text: Scrape firmly under each patty to keep the crust attached and flip. Lay a slice of cheddar on each straight away and cook until the cheese has melted.
Stack the patties in pairs and keep them warm on a plate while you cook the rest, scraping the pan clean of any burnt bits between batches.
Spread sauce on both halves of each bun. Add lettuce and a double patty to each base, top with the chopped onion and gherkin slices, then close and serve immediately.

tips: Do not use lean mince. The fat is what fries the patty from underneath and makes the crust.
No oil is needed in a seasoned cast-iron pan. In a stainless steel pan, wipe on the thinnest film of vegetable oil first.
storage: Best eaten the moment they are assembled. The sauce keeps for 5 days in the fridge.
author: Simmer
